feature_contracts.description: A syntactically valid, legal, fresh command with in-range flow summary and target shall be accepted through the input stream and generate a response indication without asserting fault-driven inhibition.

When the response side is not ready, the output valid may remain asserted while the input side remains independently backpressured only by its own readiness policy; the top-level response channel must obey ready/valid semantics.
Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface must expose a ready/response path for register access.
After reset, command validity is inhibited until a valid frame is accepted; the design does not silently substitute a command.

top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level wrapper that terminates the external command stream, the response stream, and the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface. It coordinates parsing, validation, watchdog supervision, safety clamping, command buffering, state sequencing, status reporting, and fault latching. It must be the synthesizable design top.
top_module.functionality: Accepts compact command packets on ctrl_in_data when ctrl_in_valid and ctrl_in_ready are asserted. Decodes opcode, sequence, age/timestamp, flow-condition summary, requested actuator target, and diagnostic bits. Checks legality, monotonic sequence advance, freshness, operating-envelope bounds for the 20 to 55 m/s envelope, and command-target range. Supervises a watchdog timer and sticky fault state. Applies hard clamping to the requested actuator target before any eligible actuation decision. Produces compact response frames on ctrl_out_data that acknowledge accepted frames or report fault summaries. Exposes firmware-readable and writable configuration/status registers over a small CSR/MMIO interface. On reset, initializes internal state and fault latches to a known safe and non-driving state; no actuator command validity is asserted until a valid command is accepted.
responsibilities: Terminate and backpressure the input command stream.
Decode and validate compact command frames.
Track sequence progression and freshness.
Latch stale, invalid, timeout, clamp, and communication-loss faults.
Generate response frames for accepted or faulted transactions.
Expose firmware-visible configuration and status registers.
Maintain bounded, FPGA-friendly storage for the last accepted command and its metadata.
top_module.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, clear output-valid indications, deassert input readiness until initialized, clear the response formatter state, initialize the watchdog and sequence trackers, clear sticky fault bits only if specified by CSR policy, and force the commanded-actuator-valid path to an inhibited state. No fallback command is substituted; actuator validity remains deasserted until a valid command is accepted and freshness conditions are met.
behavior_rules: Input stream handshake shall only accept ctrl_in_data when ctrl_in_valid and ctrl_in_ready are both asserted.
The controller shall not silently replace a rejected command with an alternate command; invalid, stale, timed-out, or faulted commands only result in inhibited actuator validity and fault reporting.
The response stream shall emit at most one response context per accepted frame or fault event and shall obey ctrl_out_ready backpressure.
CSR reads and writes shall be acknowledged through csr_ready and returned data through csr_rdata.
The design shall not expose tensors, large flow fields, or geometry arrays at top level.
The design shall preserve bounded command history only as required for last-accepted-command observability and status reporting.
Applied-command validity must be inhibited whenever stale_fault, invalid_frame, timeout_fault, or internal_fault is asserted.

modules.name: stream_rx_parser
modules.description: Fixed-width packet parser for compact active-aerodynamics control frames. It extracts opcode, sequence number, age/timestamp, flow-condition summary, requested actuator target, and diagnostic bits from ctrl_in_data and presents decoded semantic fields to downstream validation. It also participates in ready/valid input handshaking.
modules.functionality: Decodes a fixed packet format within the 128-bit payload limit. Asserts rx_frame_valid when the structure is syntactically acceptable and the fields can be extracted. Provides decoded semantic outputs for validation and status capture. Maintains shallow internal logic suitable for FPGA timing.
responsibilities: Parse compact command packets.
Expose decoded semantic fields to validation and status logic.
Assert parser-level frame validity for syntactic framing errors.
Support input backpressure through ready/valid.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, ctrl_in_ready and rx_frame_valid are deasserted and decoded outputs return to a benign known state until a new valid packet is accepted.
behavior_rules: The parser shall not perform learned inference, flow computation, or geometry processing.
The parser shall not widen the packet beyond 128 bits.
The parser shall only emit decoded values when the packet format is accepted as syntactically valid.
The parser shall preserve fixed bit slices per the implementation-defined packet format described by the top-level contract.

modules.name: request_validator
modules.description: Semantic and protocol validator for decoded command fields. It checks legal opcode encoding, monotonic sequence progression, freshness/age limits, flow-envelope bounds for the 20 to 55 m/s operating range, and actuator target bounds against programmable safe limits.
modules.functionality: Compares decoded packet fields to configured and tracked constraints. Produces legality flags for opcode, sequence, freshness, flow envelope, and target range, along with a composite frame_legal result. Supplies the next expected sequence value for status tracking. Does not alter the request; it only classifies it.
responsibilities: Validate opcode against supported operations.
Validate monotonic sequence advance.
Validate freshness against programmed age limits.
Validate requested flow-condition summary against the operating envelope.
Validate actuator target against programmable range.
Provide composite legality results for downstream safety logic.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, legality outputs are deasserted and legal_seq_next initializes to the expected starting sequence policy value defined by firmware configuration or design default.
behavior_rules: A frame is legal only if all component checks pass and the parser marked the frame valid.
The validator shall not silently correct illegal fields.
The validator shall not generate actuator commands.
Sequence tracking shall remain monotonic and bounded to implemented width.
Flow validation shall only cover the specified 20 to 55 m/s envelope and programmable margins if enabled by firmware.

modules.name: watchdog_timer
modules.description: Cycle counter and freshness supervisor that detects stale data and communication loss when no valid accepted frame has been observed within the programmed threshold. It provides the freshness counter and timeout indication to safety and status logic.
modules.functionality: Counts cycles since the last accepted frame pulse. Asserts stale_fault when the count exceeds the programmed stale threshold and comm_loss_fault when the inactivity condition persists per policy. Exposes the current count for observability and CSR readback.
responsibilities: Track cycles since last accepted frame.
Detect stale-data timeout.
Detect communication loss condition.
Expose watchdog count for status and MMIO readback.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, watchdog_count returns to the preload or zeroed design default according to firmware configuration, and stale_fault/comm_loss_fault are deasserted until inactivity exceeds thresholds.
behavior_rules: The counter shall advance synchronously with clk.
The timeout condition shall be derived only from accepted-frame inactivity and programmed thresholds.
The watchdog shall not substitute or generate commands.
Timeout and communication-loss indications shall be sticky only if separately specified by status logic; otherwise they reflect the live condition.

modules.name: safety_manager
modules.description: Hard safety enforcement block that clamps the requested actuator target to programmable limits, selects whether the command may be considered active, and classifies fault conditions for the response and status path. It does not synthesize a fallback command value when validity is inhibited; it only gates validity and reports the safe/inhibited condition.
modules.functionality: Computes a hard-clamped target within programmable min/max and safe-range boundaries. Reports whether clamping occurred. Deasserts actuator_valid whenever the frame is illegal, stale, timed out, or internally faulted. Assert actuator_safe when the command path is inhibited or the command is within the safe range per policy.
responsibilities: Apply hard clamp to requested actuator target.
Generate clamp-event indication.
Inhibit actuator validity on any fault or illegal frame.
Report safe-state indicator for observability and response formatting.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, clamped_target returns to a configured benign value, target_clamp_event is deasserted, actuator_valid is deasserted, and actuator_safe is asserted or returned to the design's safe-state policy until a valid frame is received.
behavior_rules: Clamping shall occur before any actuation decision.
No invalid, stale, or timed-out command may assert actuator_valid.
The block shall not silently replace the requested command with an unrelated substitute; only bounded clamping of the requested target is permitted.
When any fault is present, actuator_valid shall be deasserted even if clamping produced an in-range value.

modules.name: cmd_buffer
modules.description: Shallow FPGA-friendly storage for the last accepted command and its metadata. It captures the accepted sequence, age, flow summary, target, and diagnostic bits for readback and response formation.
modules.functionality: Stores the last accepted command and metadata in FPGA-compatible storage sized for deterministic control/status readback. Presents the latest captured values to status and response formatting logic.
responsibilities: Capture accepted command metadata.
Provide last-command observability.
Remain shallow and deterministic for FPGA implementation.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, stored command metadata is cleared to a benign known state and remains so until the first accepted frame pulse.
behavior_rules: The buffer shall store only the last accepted command metadata required by the status contract.
The buffer shall not implement a large FIFO or learned-history structure.
The buffer shall not infer ASIC-style payload memory; it is a small FPGA-friendly storage block only.

modules.name: actuator_command_fsm
modules.description: State machine that sequences through IDLE, VALID_HOLD, APPLY, and SAFE_FALLBACK-equivalent control states while enforcing the no-silent-substitution safety contract. On reset it initializes to an inhibited, non-driving state. It enables command application only when a validated, fresh command is available and all safety conditions are satisfied.
modules.functionality: Manages the control sequencing around accepted commands. Produces an accepted-frame pulse only when a validated frame transitions into the accepted state. Keeps actuator_valid_out deasserted whenever faults or freshness violations are present. Reports a compact state identifier for debug/status logic.
responsibilities: Sequence command acceptance.
Generate accepted-frame pulse for downstream storage and watchdog reset.
Maintain inhibited state on reset and during faults.
Expose compact FSM state for observability.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, the FSM enters the inhibited safe state, deasserts actuator_valid_out, deasserts accepted_frame_pulse, and initializes state_id to the reset-safe encoding.
behavior_rules: The FSM may transition to APPLY only when a validated command is present and freshness is good.
The FSM shall remain inhibited when any fault is detected.
No fallback command or substitute command shall be generated on reset or fault; instead, validity is deasserted.
The FSM shall not drive actuator validity from illegal or stale requests.

modules.name: status_regs
modules.description: Status and control register block for firmware-visible observability and configuration. It exposes sticky fault bits, applied and last accepted command values, watchdog count, accepted sequence number, and safe-state indicator, and provides programmable limits and thresholds used by the rest of the design.
modules.functionality: Implements the firmware-visible CSR/MMIO window. Decodes register addresses for configuration and status, returns read data and ready/acknowledge semantics, exposes sticky fault bits and observability fields, and supplies programmable thresholds and clamp limits to downstream logic. Every declared register is reachable through RTL decode and is not merely internal state.
responsibilities: Provide firmware-visible read/write control-plane semantics.
Expose status readback for last_command, applied_command, fault flags, watchdog count, accepted sequence number, and safe-state indicator.
Provide programmable limits and thresholds to downstream logic.
Maintain sticky fault indicators for software handling.
Ensure all declared registers are reachable via decode.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, CSR outputs are initialized to their documented defaults, sticky fault bits are cleared or set according to documented reset policy, safe_state reflects the inhibited/reset-safe condition, and configuration registers revert to default programmable values until firmware writes new values.
behavior_rules: All declared registers shall be reachable through address decode.
CSR reads shall return current status and configuration values.
CSR writes shall update only the documented writable registers.
Sticky fault bits shall remain set until cleared by firmware or explicit clear policy, if implemented.
The register block shall not replace the streaming transport; it supplements it.
The control-plane bus shall remain compact and implementation-friendly for FPGA synthesis.

top_level_connections.description: Distributed synchronous clock fanout for all submodules.
Distributed active-low reset fanout for all submodules.
Streaming input valid from host or software-side producer into the parser.
Streaming command payload into the parser.

Streaming response valid output from the top-level response formatter.
Streaming response payload output from the top-level response formatter.

inter_module_signals.description: Decoded sequence number distributed to validation and accepted-command capture logic.

inter_module_signals.description: Decoded packet age/timestamp summary forwarded to validation and status capture.

inter_module_signals.description: Decoded flow-condition summary forwarded to validation and accepted-command capture.

inter_module_signals.name: rx_frame_valid
inter_module_signals.description: Parser-level frame validity qualification into semantic validation.

inter_module_signals.description: Freshness legality from validator into the control FSM.

inter_module_signals.name: frame_legal
inter_module_signals.description: Composite legality from validator into safety and sequencing logic.

inter_module_signals.name: stale_fault
inter_module_signals.description: Live stale-data fault distributed to safety, sequencing, and sticky status.

inter_module_signals.name: comm_loss_fault

inter_module_signals.name: accepted_frame_pulse
inter_module_signals.description: Accepted-frame pulse resets freshness supervision and captures the last accepted command.

inter_module_signals.name: actuator_valid_in
inter_module_signals.description: Safety-qualified actuator validity into the control FSM.

inter_module_signals.name: buf_seq
inter_module_signals.description: Accepted sequence metadata captured in the command buffer when the frame is accepted.

inter_module_signals.name: buf_target
inter_module_signals.description: Clamped and bounded target captured as the last accepted/applied command context.

inter_module_signals.name: buf_age
inter_module_signals.description: Accepted frame age metadata captured in the command buffer.

inter_module_signals.name: buf_flow_mps
inter_module_signals.description: Accepted frame flow summary captured in the command buffer.

inter_module_signals.description: Accepted frame diagnostic bits captured in the command buffer.

inter_module_signals.name: last_age
inter_module_signals.description: Last accepted age metadata included in the compact response frame.

inter_module_signals.description: Programmable minimum actuator bound from firmware to safety logic.

inter_module_signals.description: Programmable maximum actuator bound from firmware to safety logic.

inter_module_signals.name: safe_range_min

inter_module_signals.name: safe_range_max

inter_module_signals.description: Programmable stale threshold from firmware to watchdog supervision.

inter_module_signals.description: Programmable watchdog preload from firmware to freshness supervision.
